subject: LunarHealth Dedicated Onboarding — burst guardrails & multipool roadmap

Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ready to start Dedicated onboarding — initial sizing and constraints

Thanks Jasmine — excited to get started. A couple of constraints on our side before the kickoff:

- Primary region must be us-west with us-east as failover.
- Sensitive PHI-bearing workloads will run in a private VPC segment; any telemetry sent to Redwood must be opt-in.
- Peak inference: ~1.2M tokens/minute during end-of-month payroll windows; sustained baseline ~150k tokens/min.

Attached is a quick capacity spreadsheet (current baseline telemetry) and the draft SOW your AE shared. We want to confirm estimated GPU mix and an autoscale/burst guardrail so we can sign the SOW next week.

Best,
Emma
Emma Park
Head of Platform Engineering, LunarHealth

Thanks Emma — looping in the implementation and infra leads. High-level plan:

1) Week 0 (prep): confirm SOW + sign. Procurement contact copied for contract timeline.
2) Week 1 (design): region selection & pool topology (us-west primary, us-east failover), VIP networking model for private VPC.
3) Week 2 (capacity turnup): provision dedicated pools (mix of A100-80GB + H100-80GB as suggested), internal load tests, and autoscale/burst policy tuning.
4) Week 3 (handshake & cutover): canary traffic, prefix/KV-cache priming, go/no-go.

Open items for sizing:
- Expected average sequence length for payroll flows? (affects KV cache sizing)
- SLO targets for 95th pct latency (we typically tune for <=150ms token latency at target QPS).

I've attached a mutual action plan doc and a capacity worksheet we've started. Rishi/Karthik — can you propose a default autoscale policy that limits burst to 2.5x baseline for first 90 days and includes circuit-breaker fallback to smaller quantized model variants?

Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-lunarhealth.docx (DOCX)

Thanks all — quick technical note on burst guardrails and multipool routing. Proposed defaults:

- Baseline pool sized for sustained 150k tokens/min using 8 x H100-80GB. (We recommend H100 for high token throughput for your workload.)
- Burst window: allow up to 2.5x baseline for bursts lasting up to 12 minutes with a cooldown of 30 minutes. Any sustained demand beyond that triggers pre-warm workflows and an alert to LunarHealth on-call.
- Autoscale triggers: CPU/GPU util > 65% AND queue latency > 200ms for 60s -> scale +1 worker.
- Circuit-breaker: if average latency > 500ms for 3 consecutive minutes, route to quantized variant (q4b) in a dedicated backup pool to preserve throughput.
- Cross-region failover: active-active with traffic steering based on regional latency; primary keeps stateful KV caches, failover mode warms caches via prefetch strategy during warnings.

I'll attach a short capacity calc and a sample policy snippet. Karthik, can you validate kernel/quantization compatibility for the listed models?

Rishi
Senior Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity-estimate-lunarhealth.xlsx (XLSX)

Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ready to start Dedicated onboarding — initial sizing and constraints

Looping Carlos from CloudOps for network peering and region capacity verification. Quick validation notes from infra:

- H100s are preferred for throughput; A100s are fine for cost-optimized paths but will need more nodes.
- Quantized fallback (q4b) will work on H100; for A100 we'd recommend q8_0 fallback for best perf/cost tradeoff.
- KV cache sizing: estimate ~40GB of persistence per 100k sustained tokens/minute with your median sequence length (~512). If sequence length climbs, plan +25% cache headroom.
- Network peering: we'll request a transit connection to LunarHealth VPC in us-west; Carlos, can you confirm available bandwidth and IP space mapping?

I've sketched a minimal pool topology in the shared Drive link. Carlos, recommended document to sign for peering: CloudOps-Transit-LOA.pdf (Carlos attached in reply).

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
